title: Mom's important call
setting: Evening at Kenta and Sora's flat. Sora has just got out of the bath. While he was in there, his phone kept ringing on the table.

speakers.name: Sora's mom
speakers.voice: female, 50s, lively and talkative (heard over the phone)

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: a, sora. sakki, sora no okaasan kara denwa atta yo.
lines.ja: あ、ソラ。さっき、ソラのお母さんから電話あったよ。
lines.kana: あ、そら。さっき、そらのおかあさんからでんわあったよ。
lines.english: Oh, Sora. Your mom called a little while ago.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, honto? ofuro haitteta kara, kikoenakatta.
lines.ja: え、ほんと？お風呂入ってたから、聞こえなかった。
lines.kana: え、ほんと？おふろはいってたから、きこえなかった。
lines.english: Really? I was in the bath, so I didn't hear it.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: un, zutto natteta yo. de, boku no denwa ni mo kakatte kita n da.
lines.ja: うん、ずっと鳴ってたよ。で、僕の電話にもかかってきたんだ。
lines.kana: うん、ずっとなってたよ。で、ぼくのでんわにもかかってきたんだ。
lines.english: Yeah, it kept ringing. And then she called my phone too.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, kenta ni mo denwa atta no? nande?
lines.ja: え、ケンタにも電話あったの？なんで？
lines.kana: え、けんたにもでんわあったの？なんで？
lines.english: Wait, she called you too? Why?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sora ga denwa ni denai kara tte. daiji na hanashi da kara, sugu denwa kakete tte.
lines.ja: ソラが電話に出ないからって。大事な話だから、すぐ電話かけてって。
lines.kana: そらがでんわにでないからって。だいじなはなしだから、すぐでんわかけてって。
lines.english: She said it was because you weren't picking up. It's important, so call her right away.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: daiji na hanashi? nan darou. jaa, kakete miru.
lines.ja: 大事な話？何だろう。じゃあ、かけてみる。
lines.kana: だいじなはなし？なんだろう。じゃあ、かけてみる。
lines.english: Something important? I wonder what. OK, I'll call her.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: a, mata natteru yo! hayaku dete.
lines.ja: あ、また鳴ってるよ！早く出て。
lines.kana: あ、またなってるよ！はやくでて。
lines.english: Oh, it's ringing again! Quick, answer it.

lines.speaker: sora-mom
lines.romaji: sora? yatto deta! mou, nando mo kaketa noni.
lines.ja: ソラ？やっと出た！もう、何度もかけたのに。
lines.kana: そら？やっとでた！もう、なんどもかけたのに。
lines.english: Sora? Finally, you picked up! Honestly, I called you so many times.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: gomen, ofuro haitteta. de, daiji na hanashi tte nani?
lines.ja: ごめん、お風呂入ってた。で、大事な話って何？
lines.kana: ごめん、おふろはいってた。で、だいじなはなしってなに？
lines.english: Sorry, I was in the bath. So what's the important thing?

lines.speaker: sora-mom
lines.ja: ソラ、ちゃんとご飯食べてる？
lines.kana: そら、ちゃんとごはんたべてる？

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, sore dake? tabeteru yo. jaa, kiru ne.
lines.ja: え、それだけ？食べてるよ。じゃあ、切るね。
lines.kana: え、それだけ？たべてるよ。じゃあ、きるね。
lines.english: What, that's it? Yes, I'm eating. OK, I'm hanging up.

lines.speaker: sora-mom
lines.romaji: a, matte, mada kiranaide! ato ne, kinou no koto na n da kedo.
lines.ja: あ、待って、まだ切らないで！あとね、昨日のことなんだけど。
lines.kana: あ、まって、まだきらないで！あとね、きのうのことなんだけど。
lines.english: Oh, wait, don't hang up yet! And another thing, about yesterday...

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: gomen, ima isogashii kara. jaa ne!
lines.ja: ごめん、今忙しいから。じゃあね！
lines.kana: ごめん、いまいそがしいから。じゃあね！
lines.english: Sorry, I'm busy right now. Bye!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, denwa kitchatta no? isogashikunai jan.
lines.ja: え、電話切っちゃったの？忙しくないじゃん。
lines.kana: え、でんわきっちゃったの？いそがしくないじゃん。
lines.english: What, you hung up on her? You're not busy.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: datte okaasan, hanashi nagai n da mon. ichijikan wa kirasete kurenai yo.
lines.ja: だってお母さん、話長いんだもん。一時間は切らせてくれないよ。
lines.kana: だっておかあさん、はなしながいんだもん。いちじかんはきらせてくれないよ。
lines.english: Well, Mom goes on forever. She won't let me hang up for at least an hour.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: a, kondo wa boku no denwa natteru. sora no okaasan da.
lines.ja: あ、今度は僕の電話鳴ってる。ソラのお母さんだ。
lines.kana: あ、こんどはぼくのでんわなってる。そらのおかあさんだ。
lines.english: Oh, now my phone's ringing. It's your mom.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, mata kenta ni denwa kakatte kita no? denaide!
lines.ja: え、またケンタに電話かかってきたの？出ないで！
lines.kana: え、またけんたにでんわかかってきたの？でないで！
lines.english: What, she's calling you again? Don't answer!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: moshimoshi? hai, sora nara, koko ni imasu yo.
lines.ja: もしもし？はい、ソラなら、ここにいますよ。
lines.kana: もしもし？はい、そらなら、ここにいますよ。

choices.english: Sora's mom has important news about yesterday, so Sora calls her back and they talk for an hour.
Sora's mom only wants to know if he's eating. Sora hangs up on her, and when she calls Kenta, Kenta tells her Sora is right there.
Sora can't reach his mom, so Kenta calls her for him and tells her Sora is busy.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Kenta passes on that Sora's mom called (okaasan kara denwa atta), and in line 3 she called Kenta's phone too. Line 5: she said it was important. Lines 8-10: when Sora finally picks up, the important thing is only whether he's eating properly (chanto gohan tabeteru?). Lines 11-13: she wants to keep talking (mada kiranaide), but Sora says he's busy and hangs up. Lines 16-18: she calls Kenta's phone again, Sora begs him not to answer (denaide), and Kenta answers and tells her Sora is right here (koko ni imasu yo). A is wrong: the important thing was just about eating, and Sora hangs up as soon as she starts on yesterday (line 12). The hour is how long he says she'd keep him (line 15). C is wrong: Kenta never calls her. She calls him (lines 3 and 16), and Sora is the one who says he's busy (line 13). Kenta says Sora is right there.

questions.english: You and Kenta are waiting for Yuki at a café, and she's late. Kenta says, "yuki, osoi ne. dou shita n darou." Offer to phone her, using denwa o kakeru.
questions.ja: ユキ、遅いね。どうしたんだろう。
questions.kana: ゆき、おそいね。どうしたんだろう。
questions.romaji: yuki, osoi ne. dou shita n darou.
questions.answer: Offer to try calling her: denwa kakete miru (let me try calling), with the person marked by ni if you name her (yuki ni denwa kakete miru). Phoning someone is denwa o kakeru, not yobu (that's calling someone over) and not iu.

modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと電話かけてみるね。

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, yuki ni denwa kakete miyou ka.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、ユキに電話かけてみようか。
modelAnswers.english: Shall I try calling Yuki, then?

questions.explanation: In line 5 Kenta passes on 'sugu denwa kakete' (call her right away), in line 6 Sora answers 'kakete miru' (I'll try calling her), and in line 8 his mom says 'nando mo kaketa noni' (I called you so many times). kakeru is the one you do: you make the call. When a call comes to you, it's kakaru instead (line 3: kakatte kita). kakete miru, 'try calling', is the everyday way to say it when you don't know whether they'll pick up. Kenta is a friend, so a casual answer fits.

questions.english: When Sora's phone starts ringing again, what does Kenta tell him?
questions.ja: また電話が鳴りました。ケンタは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: またでんわがなりました。けんたはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mata denwa ga narimashita. kenta wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Quick, pick it up (off the floor).

questions.explanation: Line 7: 'a, mata natteru yo! hayaku dete.' Picking up a phone is denwa ni deru, literally 'come out to the phone', and dete on its own means 'get the phone'. The same verb comes back in line 5 (denwa ni denai, you weren't picking up), line 8 (yatto deta, finally you picked up) and line 17 (denaide, don't answer). A is wrong: kotaeru is for answering a question (shitsumon ni kotaeru), not a phone. B is wrong: hirou is picking something up off the ground. The English 'pick up' doesn't carry over to phones.

questions.english: You've been chatting with Yuki on the phone late at night. She says, "a, mou juuniji da! sorosoro neru ne." Wrap up the call, using denwa o kiru.
questions.ja: あ、もう十二時だ！そろそろ寝るね。
questions.kana: あ、もうじゅうにじだ！そろそろねるね。
questions.romaji: a, mou juuniji da! sorosoro neru ne.
questions.answer: Say you'll hang up: jaa, kiru ne (OK, I'll hang up), then say good night. Ending a call is kiru, 'cut', not kakeru: kakeru starts a call.

modelAnswers.ja: うん、じゃあ切るね。おやすみ！
modelAnswers.english: OK, I'll hang up then. Night!

modelAnswers.romaji: sou da ne. jaa, denwa kiru yo. mata ashita ne.
modelAnswers.ja: そうだね。じゃあ、電話切るよ。また明日ね。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah. I'll hang up, then. Talk tomorrow.

questions.explanation: In line 11 Sora tries to end the call with exactly this phrase, 'jaa, kiru ne'. In line 12 his mom says 'mada kiranaide' (don't hang up yet), in line 14 Kenta says 'denwa kitchatta no?' (you hung up on her?), and in line 15 Sora says she won't let him hang up for an hour (kirasete kurenai). kakeru 'hang' makes the call, and kiru 'cut' ends it. Don't mix it up with kiru 'wear': hung up is kitta (kitchatta), wore is kita. Yuki is a friend, so stay casual.

questions.english: Kenta says, "a, mata natteru yo!" What has he noticed?
questions.ja: ケンタは、何に気がつきましたか？
questions.kana: けんたは、なににきがつきましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta wa, nani ni ki ga tsukimashita ka?

choices.english: Things are turning out the same way again.

questions.explanation: Line 7: natteru is (denwa ga) natteru, the phone is ringing. Kenta says mata (again) because in line 3 he told Sora it had been ringing the whole time (zutto natteta), and in line 8 Sora's mom is on the line. In line 16 Kenta uses it again for his own phone (boku no denwa natteru). B is wrong: naru does work for a doorbell too, but the next voice is Sora's mom on the phone, not someone at the door. C reads it as naru 'become' (natteru = has become). The two are said with a different pitch, and nothing 'becomes' anything here: it's the phone.

questions.english: Sora went out and left his phone at the flat. While he was gone, Yuki called it. When he gets back, he says, "a, denwa wasureteta. nanka atta?" Tell him Yuki called, using denwa ga aru.
questions.ja: あ、電話忘れてた。なんかあった？
questions.kana: あ、でんわわすれてた。なんかあった？
questions.answer: Pass on the call: yuki kara denwa atta yo, with the caller marked by kara. Not yuki ga denwa shita (that sounds like she phoned someone else) and not yuki ni denwa atta (that's a call for Yuki).

modelAnswers.romaji: un, yuki kara denwa atta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、ユキから電話あったよ。

modelAnswers.romaji: yuki kara denwa atta yo. ato de kakete hoshii tte.
modelAnswers.ja: ユキから電話あったよ。あとでかけてほしいって。
modelAnswers.english: Yuki called. She wants you to call her back later.

questions.explanation: This is what Kenta does in line 1: 'sakki, sora no okaasan kara denwa atta yo' (your mom called a little while ago). denwa ga aru reports that a call happened, to pass it on, and kara marks who called. In line 4 Sora uses ni instead (kenta ni mo denwa atta no?) because there ni marks the person the call came to. Sora is your flatmate, so a casual answer fits, and ga usually drops (denwa atta).

questions.english: Early on, Kenta tells Sora that his mom got in touch with Kenta as well. What does he say?
questions.ja: ソラのお母さんは、ケンタにも連絡しました。ケンタは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらのおかあさんは、けんたにもれんらくしました。けんたはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora no okaasan wa, kenta ni mo renraku shimashita. kenta wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.romaji: boku mo okaasan ni denwa kaketa
boku no denwa ni mo kakatte kita

questions.explanation: Line 3: 'boku no denwa ni mo kakatte kita n da.' For a call coming in to you, the call is the subject with kakaru, and -te kuru shows it coming toward you. In line 17 Sora says it again: 'mata kenta ni denwa kakatte kita no?' (she's calling you again?). A is wrong: kaketa would mean Kenta made the call himself. He never calls her. She calls him. B is wrong: yobu means calling someone over (summoning), so yobareta means 'I was called in', not a phone call.
